title: Host-bound network scoping, RBAC v2 mapping, and SIEM evidence automation playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook documents a host-bound VPC compartmentalization pattern for Private Deployments, describes RBAC v2 mappings that align with network guardrails, defines an audit-log schema for SIEM ingestion, and provides an evidence-automation runbook to produce compliance artifacts (for SOC and customer audits). Target audience: platform engineers, security engineers, and solutions engineering for Private deployments.

Summary / high level goals:
- Isolate customer workloads into host-bound compartments (per-customer subnet groups + control plane subnet).
- Enforce least privilege via RBAC v2 mapped to network operations (who can modify firewall / route / mTLS certs).
- Produce SIEM-ready audit events on every network policy and key lifecycle change.
- Automate evidence export (signed artifacts + timestamped manifests) for audits.

ASCII diagram (logical):

  Internet  --->  Edge NAT / LB  --->  Control Plane Subnet (private)  --->  Host-bound Compartment A (customer-a)
                                      |                               --->  Host-bound Compartment B (customer-b)
                                      |-- Observability / SIEM forwarder (VPC peering)

Host-bound VPC compartments (pattern):
- Compartment = a set of subnets and security group templates scoped to a single tenant or customer workload.
- Minimum subnet set per compartment: 
  - mgmt-subnet (bastion, config agents)
  - services-subnet (app/agents with mTLS enforced)
  - kvcache-subnet (stateful, restricted egress)
  - egress-proxy-subnet (controlled egress to S3, metrics endpoints)
- Each compartment has a companion route table and a security-group baseline enforced by firewall ACLs (see templates below).

Firewall rule templates (recommended starting point):
- Baseline deny-all inbound to compartment. Explicit allow rules only.
- Example ingress allow list (services-subnet):
  - Allow TCP 443 from control-plane-cidr (for config + cert bootstrap).
  - Allow 22 from mgmt-subnet (bastion) with just-in-time access and ephemeral keys.
  - Allow internal ephemeral ports (32768-61000) from same compartment for kernel/userland comms.
- Example egress allow list (egress-proxy-subnet):
  - Allow TCP 443 to S3 endpoints (prefix list) for image/patch pulls.
  - Deny direct internet access from services-subnet; route through egress-proxy-subnet.
- Stateful vs stateless: implement stateful security groups for short-lived flows, and stateless ACLs to enforce base deny for cross-compartment traffic.

mTLS provisioning and rotation (operational checklist):
- Produce per-host identity certs signed by the private-deployments CA. CA stored in KMS-backed HSM in the control plane.
- Bootstrap flow: host requests cert using signed CSR over control-plane TLS (mutual when possible).
- Minimum cert fields: CN=instance-id, O=customer-id, OU=compartment, SANs=internal-hostname.
- Rotation cadence: host certs rotate 7d default, maximum 30d for non-regulated customers. CA rotation annually with overlap window >= 7 days.
- Emergency revocation: publish CRL + push revocation list to forwarders. Also mark host as "quarantined" in inventory (see evidence automation step 4).

RBAC v2 mapping (principals, roles, resources, policies):
- Principals: human operators (SRE, Solutions Engineer), service accounts (infra-agent, cert-issuer), external integrations (sonic-siem-forwarder).
- Resources (network-focused): compartment/*, subnet/*, firewall-rule/*, route-table/*, ca/*, cert/*, siem-forwarder/*
- Example roles (canonical):
  - net-admin: full network config (compartment, firewall, routes). Assigned to small ops team, MFA + hardware token required.
  - net-operator: apply patch rules, trigger reboots, request cert issuance. Cannot modify route tables or CA.
  - cert-issuer: service account allowed to create certs under cert/* if CSR valid and host in inventory.
  - evidence-reader: read-only access to evidence manifests, audit exports.
- Policy examples (pseudocode allow/deny):
  - allow net-operator on firewall-rule/* where resource.compartment == principal.assigned_compartment
  - deny net-operator on route-table/* unless principal.has_claim("route_edit") == true
  - allow cert-issuer on cert/* if csr.signed_by == "host-agent" and host.status == "enrolled"
- Mapping to enforcement: map RBAC decisions to IAM tokens used by the control plane (JWT with claims for compartment and role). Control plane verifies via introspection hook before applying any network change.

Audit log schema (single-line JSON event example for SIEM ingestion):
- Top-level fields we require: timestamp, event_id, actor, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, compartment, before, after, request_id, ip, trace_id, outcome, evidence_manifest_id
- Example event (one-line JSON string):
  {"timestamp":"2026-02-10T14:32:01Z","event_id":"evt-9c3a","actor":"ethan.park@redwood.com","actor_type":"human","action":"update_firewall_rule","resource_type":"firewall-rule","resource_id":"fr-84","compartment":"customer-a","before":"{"src":"0.0.0.0/0","dst":"443","action":"deny"}","after":"{"src":"10.0.0.0/8","dst":"443","action":"allow"}","request_id":"req-159a","ip":"34.86.21.44","trace_id":"trace-7f12","outcome":"success","evidence_manifest_id":"em-20260210-84"}

SIEM export mapping (fields -> SIEM/ECS suggestions):
- timestamp -> @timestamp
- event_id -> event.id
- actor -> user.email / user.name
- actor_type -> user.type
- action -> event.action
- resource_type -> event.module (custom: redwood_network)
- resource_id -> network.firewall.rule.id
- compartment -> tags.customer_compartment
- before/after -> message or network.firewall.change.before/after (stringified)
- request_id -> event.ingested_from.request_id
- ip -> source.ip
- trace_id -> trace.id
- outcome -> event.outcome

Evidence automation runbook (producing an artifact set for audits):
1) Trigger: nightly evidence job or ad-hoc (audit request).
2) Steps:
   a) Snapshot network configuration: collect API responses for compartment/*, subnet/*, firewall-rule/*, route-table/* (timestamped).
   b) Snapshot RBAC policy and assignments for the last 90 days that touched network resources (include JWT claims used at time of change).
   c) Collect CA signing logs and cert issuance events (cert/*) for the period.
   d) Collect SIEM export subset (events where resource_type startswith "firewall" or "route") and output as gzipped ndjson.
   e) Produce manifest.json: {"id":"em-<date>-<rand>","collected_at":"<ts>","sha256":{file:hash,..},"signed_by":"<owner>"} (manifest must be signed by a key in HSM and include human-ack).
   f) Push artifacts to evidence-bucket with restricted ACL and record object URLs in the manifest.
3) Verification queries (sample):
   - ES/Kibana KQL: event.module: "redwood_network" and event.action: "update_firewall_rule" and outcome: "success" | sort @timestamp desc | limit 100
   - SQL on config-store: select * from firewall_rules where compartment = 'customer-a' and updated_at > '2026-02-01'
4) Post-processing: generate a signed PDF summary for auditors containing a) scope, b) checklist passed/failed, c) artifact URLs, d) contact.

Playbook checklist (quick):
- [ ] All compartments have baseline deny-all applied
- [ ] mTLS certs issued via CA, enrollment proofs present in evidence manifest
- [ ] RBAC mappings exported and reviewed by SRE/security (last 30 days)
- [ ] SIEM ingestion validated (sample events present for network changes)
- [ ] Evidence artifacts signed and stored with ACLs
- [ ] Egress proxy enforced for services-subnet
- [ ] JIT bastion used for mgmt-subnet access

Acceptance criteria for Private Deploy readiness (minimal):
- Automated daily evidence job runs without errors for 7 consecutive days.
- Any firewall change generates an audit event within 10s and is forwarded to SIEM.
- Cert issuance events include request_id traceability back to host inventory and RBAC claim used.
- Emergency revocation shows host marked quarantined in inventory and evidence manifest entry created.

Known gaps / open questions:
- How should multi-tenant control plane operators be logically segregated in RBAC when they manage multiple customers? (current suggestion: constrain by compartment claims, but need hardened attestation and approval flows).
- Need to finalize event schema versioning semantics (version field in audit event?).
- Decide if CRL or OCSP is primary revocation mechanism for air-gapped customer variants.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- curl to fetch firewall rules (control plane API):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/firewall-rules?compartment=customer-a | jq '.'

- sample manifest signing (HSM-backed signer placeholder):
  SIGNED=$(cat manifest.json | hsm-sign --key-id projects/ca-key-1)
  gsutil cp manifest.json gs://evidence-bucket/em-20260210-84/manifest.json
  gsutil cp ${SIGNED} gs://evidence-bucket/em-20260210-84/manifest.sig

References and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/company/private-deploy-hostbound-v1
- RFC: internal/rfc/network-compartment-pattern.md (draft)
- Jira epic: JIRA-PLAT-8421

Notes to reviewers (short):
- This is intentionally prescriptive but still conservative; the goal is to provide a reproducible audit trail and straightforward SIEM mapping rather than a perfect one-size-fits-all policy.
- If you are implementing for an air-gapped customer, call out CRL/OCSP choice and provide an alternate evidence export mechanism (USB-handoff process).
